_doc: Plain words on what each step of a necklace actually uses, shown after its summary on the page, llms.txt, the MCP tool, the A2A skill and /api/necklaces (PM 11-16: the summary is part of the judged definition and cannot change before a new gate, so a summary that reads wider than the sources is corrected here). Facts from the workflow team for the version judged; update this line whenever the members of a step change. Keys are necklace slugs. A value may also be an object: {'sources': sentence, 'accuracy_scope': where the accuracy was measured (added next to the accuracy in the measured line), 'attribution': {'text': ..., 'links': [{'label', 'url' (https)}]} for a source whose terms require it}. Shown only while the necklace is offered.
topic-evidence-brief: What each step uses (as of 2026-11-17): the web step answers from English Wikipedia, quoting the lead sentences of the best-matching articles with links (not a web search); the background step summarises the one Wikipedia article on the topic, so both come from Wikipedia; papers come from two third-party paper search agents (one of them uses OpenAlex; neither is verified yet), and from our own Crossref search only when both fail; news is optional.

attribution.text: Based on data from MET Norway.

weather-outdoor-brief._note: Agent team 11-16 (PM decision): the met-weather step is checked against US NWS forecasts on 30 US points only; other regions are checked for form and freshness. MET Norway terms require the attribution and licence links. Gate 11-19~20; add a sources sentence when the members are known.
